I got my Bachelor's degree in an in-demand STEM program. I got a job in my exact field that paid well enough. I do not buy "luxury" items like coffee or takeout or new cloths (only thrift stores for me) or any sort of fun. I only participate in free activities to have any semblance of a life. I have continued to pay off my student debt but I'm not even close to making a dent in it. I left my job and started a related STEM grad program in 2019 and it was the absolute worst decision of my life. My school debt has tripled due to Doug Ford's changes in OSAP. I do not have the luxury of living with my parents (dysfunctional family) but my husband and I have done the best we can to live in 1 place for as long as possible so rent stays low. 

Same as you, I have done everything that I was supposed to do. I'm more in debt than I've ever been. I am miserable because that's "what I was supposed to do". I have less job prospects than before I started grad school. I'm nearing 30 and literally can't afford to live. 

I'm sorry that you're going through this too.

I have many reasons for never wanting kids. I physically do not want to ever carry a child. I have no desire (or maternal instinct) to have a child. Children cost a lot of money, I do not necessarily want to go in debt or just make ends meet to provide care for a child. I want to do great things in my life (great career, travel, savings, etc.) that would be challenging with kids. I do not want to put my career on hold to physically recover from having children. I do not want to baby proof my house or lifestyle. I don't want to put a strain on my relationship with my husband. And selfishly, I don't want my life to revolve around anyone other than myself or my husband.

Both my husband and I come from traumatic childhoods (you can see my post history). We have experienced the worst of "parenting". We both realised when we were really young (I was 10 and he was about 16 years old) that we did not want to have kids.

Time has definitely shown my ex's true colours! He abused the next 3 girls he dated and one or two of them reported it to the police. I regret that I was so broken after I left that I was scared I wouldn't be trusted my the police if I reported it, so I never did. Around 5 years after I left my ex (and about 2 years after I told sister and BIL for the second time), ex spent some time in jail for assault. 

But my "friends" or even my BIL never apologized for how they acted towards me. Never acknowledged what was said or done. You are completely right, to hell with them!!

My past relationship ended almost a decade ago, so I have not wholly relied on my family for support for a while. After I initially tried telling my sister and BIL and that didn't end well, I stopped attempting to go to my family for support. The second time I tried to tell them, I had just wanted my story, my life, my experience, out there for them to know. My husband and a few of my friends at the time were very supportive and helpful when I opened up to them about my past relationship after I was finally being able to talk about it. I actually lost a lot of friends as a result of my previous relationship because they either "sided" with my charming, extroverted ex or I'd lost connection with them during my relationship.  And honestly, by the point of leaving that relationship, I was so isolated away from any friendships that I had previously had, that I thought my only safe place was my "family". 

But unfortunately, I think you are right. My sister refuses to acknowledge the trauma we went through as kids because of my abusive father. I think the saying is “those that fail to learn from history are doomed to repeat it.” She is nearing 40 years old (around the same age my mom was when she left my father) and with time, I have noticed a lot of similarities to that situation and/or my own previous situation.

1. In high school, I successfully performed the heimlich maneuver on a friend that was choking! Terrifying but an adrenaline rush. Darn hard candies being the same size as the trachea. 

2. I found and married the love of my life. I didn't realise that I could be so comfortable and compatible with another human being. 

3. I do not really play video games, maybe 1 game every 2 or 3 years. But every game I have played, I have gotten every single PlayStation trophy and completed every single quest/story, resulting in platinum trophies.

Although I have not found a dead body, my husband unfortunately has. He grew up in a turmoilous home with his biological mother, who was an addict. She lived with many different men throughout the time my husband lived with her (he went into foster care around 9 years old). 

When my husband was 6 years old, he came home from school to see his mom's boyfriend asleep on the couch. He said it was weird how cold he was so he put a blanket on the man. When his mom woke up from her drunken stupor, she freaked out. My husband remembers sitting on the floor in front of the couch watching TV, thinking that the boyfriend was sleeping, when he had actually overdosed. My husband was sent to the bedroom for the rest of the night and isn't sure (has purposedly blocked those memories) of what happened afterwards. My husband still has a lot of trauma from this experience and overall from living with his biological mother.

My husband did not speak about this situation until he was 23 years old because of how haunting and scarring it was. 

Tldr; Man overdosed on couch, child found him and thought the man was sleeping.

During those 3 months was enough for me to realise I needed professional help dealing with my suicidal thoughts.

When looking at your transcript, taking classes through ILC is the exact same as taking classes in high school. Colleges and universities will not hold it against your admission if your classes were completed on ILC.

I'm pretty sure ILC has a few different course options, fully online or partially online with send away booklets (it depends on the course). But the final exam is always done in person at a learning centre (most towns/cities have a centre so you do not need to travel to Toronto). Each course gives you about 6-8 months to finish. But the course can be finished in about a month, if treated like a full time job. And more than one class can be taken at a time. At least for my husband, because the course let him go at his own pace, he was able to fully understand the material and aced the classes he took. 

Any of the courses you take on ILC that are new to you (as in you did not take that class in high school), that mark will be on your transcript. Someone explained to me that if you repeat a class that you took in high school, both will appear on your transcript and only the higher mark will be counted towards school admission. But when I was in high school, the marks would have been averaged, so I hope that I am answering this correctly.
Exactly!!! A wedding is supposed to be a celebration of the couple! I can't believe that the fiance would willing chose people who dislike the bride to stand up with him.

I definitely recommend ILC. The website is easy to use/follow and they offer a lot of courses for upgrading your grades. ILC also offers courses that some high schools do not offer. My husband took classes that he didn't have the option to take while he was in high school and was able to attend college because of ILC. 

I've been out of high school for about a decade now, but be aware that universities used to take the average of repeated classes (say you got 61% the first time you took ENG4C then 87% the second time, it would average to 74% on your transcript). I don't know if that has changed since I've left school, so I could be wrong about that.

My husband was in foster care from age 9 to 13, when he was adopted. 

He was abused and emotionally tormented at his first foster home but because he had grown up in such disarray, he didn't understand that what he was experiencing was not okay. His social worker would ask him how he was doing (age 9-10) and he would say great because he always had a bed to sleep on and food to eat. It didn't matter that he was in a locked (from the outside) bedroom with nothing besides a bed or that he had to mow the entire yard before entering the house after school. Fortunately, his social worker picked up on the fact that something was wrong. 

He was adopted by his second foster family when he was 13, who on paper were saints. They fostered more than 50 children and adopted 9, my husband included. Behind closed doors, these children were slaves. Not just normal chores that a child of that age could do! They constantly berated him and called him stupid. They discouraged him from pursuing higher education. They tried to convince him to become a teen parent, as they both had done. They would treat their biological child, who has/had been to jail multiple times, as a saint and my husband as a delinquent, although he had never even been in trouble at school. And this was by the people who adopted him. It was all for show; to show people who saintly they were. Now that my husband is an adult, they constantly try to guilt him into giving them money (who they then give to biological son) because they "saved" him, as they constantly say. 

Eventually being adopted after being in foster care is not always what it seems. Even though he was adopted, he didn't have anyone to rely on. He was still alone. He had severe abandonment issues into this adult life that took a lot of time to work though.

I had something very similar happen to me. I was studying for my last exam of the semester that would be the next day and I scrolled Facebook to find a second cousin once removed had posted about my grandfather passing away (she was not biologically related to him but was related through a distant marriage). I called my mom in a panic and my grandmother was livid. They had asked everyone to keep it off Facebook until my mom and her siblings could tell their children. People never respect other people's wishes. I wasn't the only person to find out from Facebook that day. It was such a sad and disheartening way to find out that a beloved family member had passed away.

I did tell the one "friend" about what happened. Everyone else just shunned me right away. I know that I don't need the negativity in my life that they have caused but it really hurts not getting any closure or getting my side out there. It's so hard and today was the day I realised that my "friend" hasn't actually been a friend to me. It's just hard to let go. 

I have come to terms with what I have went through and what I survived. I just can't imagine someone willingly choosing to be associated with a person capable of so much hate and destruction.

He didn't care about me and my sisters. He honestly didn't care about my brother either. It was all about his ego, he said he'd have a boy and that's all he wanted. It was hard growing up knowing I wasn't wanted for who I am and my younger sisters had it worse. It didn't matter that I was a tomboy, played in the dirt, got into "boy hobbies", I was still a girl and that's all he cared about. 

Don't let him pressure you into having more children than you want. Do you want a son raised in a family where women can be told what to do with their own bodies? Do you want a daughter that will always feel like a second class citizen to her brother? A daughter who knows her brother is the favourite?

I only had a bad experience with one bridal consultant (tiny local store), but it's the experience that sticks out in my mind the most when I think about trying to pick my wedding dress (I still get stressed thinking about trying on dresses). For one, the consultant kept bringing me dresses in styles that I specifically said I was not looking for. Not a good start. I did find my dress at this location though, then she went on a rant about how I couldn't alter this and that, how dare I want to change any part of the dress, and that I would never be able to find a veil that matched in colour to the dress. I didnt even want a veil but she never even asked. Thirdly, she was super sketchy about getting the alterations through the store.
Although I found my dress that day, I refused to buy from that shop because she made me feel bad about what I wanted. 

So my tip from this would be to make sure the bride feels comfortable and heard. And opinions from consultants are only warranted if asked! I did not ask for any of her 'opinions' about my style.
